glance_notes.source_name: Wisconsin Elections Commission — Register to Vote
glance_notes.text: Election Day Registration Available: Wisconsin allows eligible voters to register at their polling place on Election Day. A person registering must provide an acceptable proof-of-residence document. Wisconsin therefore does not have an absolute pre-election voter registration cutoff.

glance_notes.source_name: Wisconsin Elections Commission — Bring It to the Ballot
glance_notes.text: Photo ID Required to Vote: Wisconsin voters generally must present an acceptable photo ID before receiving a ballot. The address on the photo ID does not need to be current, and the ID used to prove identity for voting is separate from the proof-of-residence requirement for voter registration.

In-Person Absentee Voting Before Election Day: Wisconsin does not operate a uniform statewide early-voting schedule. Instead, voters may cast an absentee ballot in person at locations authorized by their municipal clerk. In-person absentee voting may begin no earlier than 14 days before Election Day, and exact dates, locations and hours vary by municipality.

register.label: Register to Vote
register.content: Eligible Wisconsin residents may register online when they meet the online-registration requirements, by mail, through their municipal clerk or at their polling place on Election Day. To vote from a Wisconsin address, a person generally must have resided at that address for at least 28 consecutive days before Election Day. A voter who has lived at a new Wisconsin address for fewer than 28 days generally votes using the voter's previous qualifying Wisconsin residence. Proof of residence is required when registering. Eligible voters registering online must have a current and valid Wisconsin driver license or Wisconsin state identification card with information that can be matched to Wisconsin Department of Transportation records.
register.glance_value: Online, mail, clerk or Election Day registration
register.source_name: Wisconsin Elections Commission — Register to Vote
register.internal_note: Wisconsin has a 28-day residency requirement and Election Day registration. Proof of residence is required for registration. Online registration through MyVote requires a qualifying Wisconsin driver license or state ID and a successful DMV data match. If the match fails, MyVote can generate a registration form that must be printed and submitted with proof of residence.

check_registration.label: Check Voter Registration
check_registration.content: Use MyVote Wisconsin to check voter registration, view voter information, update a name or address when eligible, review voting history, request an absentee ballot and track an absentee ballot. MyVote can also provide voter-specific polling-place and ballot information.
check_registration.source_name: Wisconsin Elections Commission — My Voter Information
check_registration.internal_note: MyVote is the official Wisconsin Elections Commission voter portal. Voters who change their legal name or residential address must submit a new voter registration rather than simply editing the existing record.

deadlines.label: Registration Deadlines
deadlines.content: Wisconsin provides several voter-registration periods and allows Election Day registration. Online and mail registration close before an election under state law, followed by a period when voters may register through their municipal clerk. Eligible voters who have not registered before Election Day may register at their assigned polling place on November 3, 2026. Election Day registrants must provide acceptable proof of residence.
deadlines.source_name: Wisconsin Elections Commission — Register to Vote
deadlines.internal_note: Do not present Wisconsin's advance registration cutoff as the final registration deadline because Wisconsin permits Election Day registration. The ordinary online/mail registration deadline is the third Wednesday before an election. Municipal-clerk registration resumes after the closed-registration period and continues through the Friday before Election Day under Wisconsin law. For voters, the most important fact is that eligible residents can still register at the polls on Election Day with proof of residence.

polling_place.label: Find a Polling Place
polling_place.content: Use MyVote Wisconsin to find your assigned Election Day polling place. Polling places are based on the voter's residential address, and MyVote provides the location, hours, directions and voter-specific ballot information. Polling locations can change, so voters should check MyVote shortly before Election Day or contact their municipal clerk.
polling_place.glance_value: Find your assigned polling place through MyVote
polling_place.source_name: Wisconsin Elections Commission — Find My Polling Place
polling_place.internal_note: MyVote expressly states that the assigned polling place is based on where the voter lives. Wisconsin does not generally use a statewide countywide-vote-center model on Election Day, so voters should use their assigned polling location.

election_day.label: Election Day Voting
election_day.content: Wisconsin's General Election is Tuesday, November 3, 2026. Polling places are open from 7:00 a.m. until 8:00 p.m. Voters who are in line at 8:00 p.m. are permitted to vote. Wisconsin voters generally must present an acceptable photo ID before receiving a ballot. Eligible residents who are not yet registered may register at their polling place on Election Day by providing acceptable proof of residence.
election_day.internal_note: Wisconsin has uniform Election Day polling hours of 7:00 a.m.-8:00 p.m. Photo ID is required to receive a regular ballot, while proof of residence is separately required for a person registering at the polls. Do not conflate these two document requirements.

polling_hours.label: Polling Hours
polling_hours.content: Wisconsin polling places are open from 7:00 a.m. until 8:00 p.m. on Election Day. A voter who is in line when the polls close at 8:00 p.m. may remain in line and vote.
polling_hours.source_name: Wisconsin Elections Commission — Find My Polling Place
polling_hours.internal_note: Wisconsin's statewide Election Day hours are 7:00 a.m.-8:00 p.m. MyVote provides the polling-place hours associated with the voter's address.

early_voting.label: In-Person Absentee Voting
early_voting.content: Wisconsin allows voters to cast an absentee ballot in person before Election Day without providing an excuse. This process is commonly called early voting but is legally in-person absentee voting. It takes place at the municipal clerk's office or another location authorized by the municipality. In-person absentee voting may begin no earlier than 14 days before Election Day. Municipalities determine their specific dates, locations and hours within state-law limits, so voters should check MyVote or contact their municipal clerk for the November 2026 schedule.
early_voting.glance_value: Begins no earlier than 14 days before Election Day; local schedules vary
early_voting.internal_note: MyVote currently states that voters can request and vote an absentee ballot in person beginning two weeks before Election Day and potentially through the Sunday before the election, with hours and availability varying by municipality. Do not fabricate a uniform statewide early-voting period. Wisconsin statutes limit the beginning and ending of in-person absentee voting, while municipalities choose schedules within those limits.

absentee_mail.label: Absentee Voting by Mail
absentee_mail.content: Any registered Wisconsin voter may request an absentee ballot without providing an excuse. Most voters may request a ballot through MyVote or submit a written request to their municipal clerk. A qualifying photo ID must generally be on file with the clerk or accompany the absentee request unless an exception applies. Completed absentee ballots must be received by the municipal clerk no later than 8:00 p.m. on Election Day. A postmark by Election Day is not sufficient if the ballot arrives after the deadline. Voters should mail completed ballots early enough to ensure timely delivery or use another return method permitted under current Wisconsin law.
absentee_mail.glance_value: No excuse required; ballot must arrive by 8:00 p.m. Election Day
absentee_mail.source_name: Wisconsin Elections Commission — Absentee Ballot Services
absentee_mail.internal_note: Wisconsin absentee ballots are subject to an Election Day receipt deadline, not merely a postmark deadline. Current MyVote supports online absentee requests and tracking. Photo ID upload may be required for an absentee request. Wisconsin absentee-ballot return rules have been heavily litigated and legislated, particularly concerning drop boxes and assistance returning ballots, so specific return-location claims should be reverified against current 2026 WEC guidance immediately before publication.

voter_id.label: Voter ID Requirements
voter_id.content: Wisconsin generally requires voters to present an acceptable photo ID before receiving a ballot. Accepted identification includes qualifying Wisconsin driver licenses and state ID cards, certain U.S. military and veterans IDs, U.S. passports, qualifying tribal identification, certain Wisconsin college or university student IDs accompanied by separate enrollment verification, and other identification authorized by state law. The address shown on the photo ID does not need to match the voter's current address. Certain IDs may be expired if they expired after the date of the most recent General Election. A voter who cannot present acceptable photo ID at the polling place may cast a provisional ballot and provide the required identification by the statutory deadline after Election Day.
voter_id.source_name: Wisconsin Elections Commission — Bring It to the Ballot
voter_id.internal_note: Wisconsin's photo-ID rule is an identity requirement, not proof of current address. An acceptable ID may therefore show an old address or no address. Student ID rules are narrower than in many states: qualifying Wisconsin college/university IDs must meet statutory requirements and generally be accompanied by proof of current enrollment. A voter lacking acceptable ID can vote provisionally and generally has until 4:00 p.m. on the Friday after Election Day to provide the required identification to the municipal clerk.

accessible_voting.label: Accessible Voting
accessible_voting.content: Wisconsin voters have the right to cast a ballot privately and independently. Polling places are required to meet applicable accessibility standards, and accessible voting equipment is provided for voters who need it. A voter who needs assistance marking a ballot because of a disability may select an eligible person to assist. Voters should contact their municipal clerk for current information about the accessibility features at their assigned polling place and available accommodations.
accessible_voting.glance_value: Accessible polling places, equipment and voter assistance
accessible_voting.source_name: Wisconsin Elections Commission — Polling Place Accessibility
accessible_voting.internal_note: Current MyVote guidance states that Wisconsin voters have a right to cast ballots privately and independently and that HAVA requires polling places to meet ADA accessibility standards. Municipal clerks have the most current polling-place accessibility information. Avoid promising a particular equipment model at every polling place.

military_overseas.label: Military & Overseas Voting
military_overseas.content: Wisconsin provides special absentee-voting procedures for eligible military voters and U.S. citizens living overseas. Qualifying voters may use federal voting forms and Wisconsin's military and overseas voter services to request absentee ballots. For elections containing a federal contest, qualifying active-duty military voters and eligible spouses or dependents may receive an absentee ballot by email, fax or mail through 5:00 p.m. on Election Day. Overseas voters and other covered voters have category-specific registration, request and return rules, so voters should use the current Wisconsin Elections Commission instructions for the November 3, 2026 General Election.
military_overseas.glance_value: Special military and overseas absentee procedures available
military_overseas.source_name: Wisconsin Elections Commission — MyVote Military & Overseas Voters
military_overseas.internal_note: MyVote's current 2026 guidance expressly states that for elections with a federal contest, active-duty U.S. military members and eligible spouses or dependents may receive an absentee ballot by email, fax or mail until 5:00 p.m. Election Day. Wisconsin distinguishes military electors from permanent and temporary overseas electors, and their deadlines are not identical. Do not collapse all UOCAVA categories into one deadline.

student_voting.label: College / Student Voting
student_voting.content: College students may register in Wisconsin if they meet the state's voter eligibility and 28-day residency requirements. A student who has lived at a Wisconsin campus or other Wisconsin address for at least 28 consecutive days before Election Day and considers that address the student's voting residence may register there. Wisconsin accepts certain student photo identification cards for voting, but the ID must satisfy specific requirements and generally must be accompanied by a separate document showing current enrollment. A student registering to vote must also provide acceptable proof of residence.
student_voting.glance_value: 28-day residency rule; qualifying student ID may be used with enrollment proof
student_voting.source_name: Wisconsin Elections Commission — Bring It to the Ballot
student_voting.internal_note: Wisconsin student voting rules require careful wording. Not every college ID qualifies as voter photo ID. A qualifying student ID from an accredited Wisconsin university or college must satisfy statutory issuance/expiration/signature requirements and be accompanied by separate proof of current enrollment. The student's residence must independently satisfy Wisconsin's 28-day rule.

sample_ballot.label: Official Sample Ballot
sample_ballot.content: Use MyVote Wisconsin to view the sample ballot associated with your residential address when ballots become available. Ballots vary by municipality, ward and political district. For elections with federal contests, MyVote states that sample ballots are typically available about 47 days before Election Day. Voters should use their own address to retrieve the ballot that applies to them.
sample_ballot.glance_value: View your voter-specific sample ballot through MyVote
sample_ballot.internal_note: MyVote currently states that ballots are typically available 47 days before an election with federal contests and 21 days before state/local contests. The November 3, 2026 General Election contains federal contests, so voter-specific sample ballots should become available well before Election Day. Reverify once final ballots are populated.

contact.label: Contact the State Election Authority
contact.content: Wisconsin Elections Commission, 201 W Washington Avenue, 2nd Floor, Madison, WI 53703. Mailing address: P.O. Box 7984, Madison, WI 53707. Phone: 608-266-8005. Toll-free: 866-VOTE-WIS. Fax: 608-267-0500. Email: elections@wi.gov. Office hours are generally Monday through Friday, 7:30 a.m. to 4:30 p.m. For voter-specific registration, absentee-ballot and polling-place questions, voters should contact their municipal clerk.
contact.source_name: Wisconsin Elections Commission — MyVote Contact Information
contact.internal_note: Current MyVote pages verify the office address, mailing address, 608-266-8005, 866-VOTE-WIS, fax 608-267-0500 and [elections@wi.gov](mailto:elections@wi.gov). MyVote's polling-place page lists office hours as Monday-Friday 7:30 a.m.-4:30 p.m. The email address is intentionally plain text with no Markdown or mailto wrapper.

official_resources.label: Official State & Local Resources
official_resources.content: Use the Wisconsin Elections Commission, MyVote Wisconsin and your municipal clerk for official election information. These resources provide voter registration, registration lookup, polling-place information, voter-specific sample ballots, absentee-ballot requests and tracking, voter photo-ID information, accessibility information and military and overseas voting services. Wisconsin elections are administered locally by municipal clerks, with county clerks and the Wisconsin Elections Commission performing additional election-administration responsibilities.
official_resources.glance_value: Wisconsin Elections Commission, MyVote & municipal clerks
official_resources.internal_note: Official Wisconsin Elections Commission voter portal: [https://myvote.wi.gov/](https://myvote.wi.gov/). Official registration page: [https://myvote.wi.gov/en-us/Register-To-Vote](https://myvote.wi.gov/en-us/Register-To-Vote). Official registration lookup: [https://myvote.wi.gov/en-us/My-Voter-Information](https://myvote.wi.gov/en-us/My-Voter-Information). Official polling-place lookup: [https://myvote.wi.gov/en-us/Find-My-Polling-Place](https://myvote.wi.gov/en-us/Find-My-Polling-Place). Official voter-specific ballot lookup: [https://myvote.wi.gov/en-us/My-Ballot](https://myvote.wi.gov/en-us/My-Ballot). Official absentee-ballot tracking and request services: [https://myvote.wi.gov/en-us/Track-My-Ballot](https://myvote.wi.gov/en-us/Track-My-Ballot).
